goal_text: Understand the core ideas behind RLHF

nodes.title: What is a language model, really?
nodes.one_liner: Neural nets, training vs. inference, and text prediction — the minimum background.

nodes.title: Why base models aren't enough
nodes.one_liner: The alignment problem RLHF exists to solve: helpful, honest, harmless outputs.

nodes.title: Stage 1: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
nodes.one_liner: Teaching a base model to follow instructions from human examples.

nodes.title: Stage 2: The reward model
nodes.one_liner: How human preference comparisons become a scoring signal for outputs.

nodes.title: Stage 3: Optimizing against the reward
nodes.one_liner: What 'policy' and PPO mean, and just enough RL to follow along.

nodes.title: The RLHF vocabulary cheat sheet
nodes.one_liner: Reward hacking, KL penalty, preference data, and other paper terms.

nodes.title: Where RLHF falls short
nodes.one_liner: Known limits and newer alternatives like DPO and RLAIF.

outline.rationale: The user is new to ML but wants to follow papers/discussions, so the outline prioritizes conceptual shape and vocabulary over math or implementation. Node 1 supplies the bare-minimum ML foundation (LM, neural net, train vs. inference) they confirmed they lack. Node 2 frames the motivating problem. Nodes 3–5 walk the canonical three-stage RLHF pipeline (SFT, reward model, RL optimization), with the RL node deliberately scoped to 'just enough' rather than full policy-optimization theory, matching the deprioritization. Node 6 is a pure terminology node serving the 'terminology fluency' goal directly. Node 7 covers criticisms and modern alternatives (DPO, RLAIF) that dominate current discussions/papers, essential for someone whose goal is to keep up with the conversation. No intro/conclusion filler; no deep RL math; no build-it-yourself content.
